title: P0: Sanitize checkout 500 error messages (audit 3.2)
description: Audit finding 3.2 (MEDIUM, P0 per coordinator): app/api/checkout/route.ts:139-144 returns raw error.message to clients on 500, leaking Stripe/Supabase internals. Log full error server-side, return generic 'Unable to start checkout.' for 500. Existing 401 and 400 responses are already sanitized — leave them alone. File: app/api/checkout/route.ts.

title: P0: Reinstate Today refresh cap for free tier (audit 2.2)
description: Audit finding 2.2 (MEDIUM, P0 per coordinator): lib/access.ts:115 sets todayRefreshesPerDay: null with a DEBUG comment from a prior tuning experiment. Set to 3 and remove the DEBUG comment. File: lib/access.ts.

title: P0: Add server-side usage limits for Ask and Today (audit 1.4)
description: Audit finding 1.4 (HIGH): lib/client-usage-limits.ts tracks free-tier limits in localStorage only. Mirror the limits server-side: 3 Ask/day, 1 big-decision/week, and Today refresh cap (see audit 2.2). Enforce in API routes BEFORE LLM dispatch using Supabase counter (per-user-per-day). Files: relevant /api routes for Ask + generate-briefing + ask-follow-up; new helper for daily counters; possible new SQL migration if a counter table is needed.

title: P0: Lock debug access override behind explicit env var (audit 1.3)
description: Audit finding 1.3 (HIGH): lib/debug-access.ts:67-69 enables cookie/header access-level override whenever NODE_ENV !== 'production'. This means staging/preview/test envs accept attacker-set wuwu_debug_access_level cookies/headers. Change isDebugAccessOverrideEnabled() to require process.env.DEBUG_ACCESS_ENABLED === 'true'. Default disabled. File: lib/debug-access.ts.

title: P0: Harden ops auth with constant-time compare and HMAC cookie (audit 1.1)
description: Audit finding 1.1 (CRITICAL): lib/ops-auth.ts uses plaintext === comparison and stores OPS_SECRET as the cookie value verbatim. Replace with HMAC-SHA256(server_secret, OPS_SECRET) as the cookie value, compared via crypto.timingSafeEqual. Must remain Edge-compatible (Web Crypto API, no Node-only imports). Files: lib/ops-auth.ts, app/ops-login/* (cookie issuance call site).

title: P1: Populate CLAUDE.md with build, test, and architecture overview (audit 4.6)
description: Audit 4.6 (CONCERN). CLAUDE.md is essentially empty (placeholder _Add your..._ sections). Populate with: build command (npm run build), typecheck (npm run typecheck), test commands (npm run test:smoke:* — note --headed/interactive), brief architecture overview (auth via Supabase Auth + bearer; billing via Stripe webhook + Supabase app_metadata; safety stack — crisis detection + output safety classifier + care mode + prompt rules; generation flow — SSE streams from /api/generate-* with two-pass routing). Also add: list of safety-critical files (lib/ops-auth.ts, lib/auth.ts, lib/billing.ts, lib/access.ts, lib/debug-access.ts, middleware.ts) that need extra care.

title: P1: Server-side age gate in onboarding submit (audit 3.3)
description: Audit 3.3 (LOW). lib/validations.ts validateOnboardingInput doesn't cross-reference birth date against the 18+ age gate. A bypassed client age gate could submit birthDate=2020-01-01. Add isAtLeastAge(input.birthDate, AGE_GATE_MINIMUM_AGE) check in the onboarding server action using the existing age-gate.ts logic.

title: P1: Sign CHECKOUT_ACCESS_COOKIE to prevent privilege escalation (audit 2.4)
description: Audit 2.4 (MEDIUM). lib/debug-access.ts:50-65 getCheckoutAccessLevelBridge respects the unsigned wuwu_checkout_access_level cookie to upgrade access on confirmation pages. An attacker setting wuwu_checkout_access_level=internal can grant internal access in production (debug override is now off in prod after audit 1.3, but the checkout bridge is always active). Sign with HMAC-SHA256 like ops auth, validate it can only escalate to 'pro', never 'internal'.

title: P1: Billing activatedNow race condition (audit 2.3)
description: Audit 2.3 (MEDIUM). lib/billing.ts:57 grantProAccessToUser computes activatedNow via read→compare→update. Concurrent webhook deliveries can both pass the check and double-fire pro_activated events / conversion pixels. Use a conditional update that checks current billing_status before setting it to active, or atomic UPSERT.
close_reason: Effectively addressed by audit 1.5 / beads-p3m. The activatedNow race condition's documented retry-of-same-event path is closed by the new event_id unique claim in stripe_webhook_events. Only checkout.session.completed calls grantProAccessToUser, and Stripe emits one such event per checkout — no two-different-events-upgrade-same-user concurrency path exists in the current handler. If a future change adds new pro-grant paths, revisit.

title: P1: Billing user lookup pagination guard (audit 1.7)
description: Audit 1.7 (MEDIUM). lib/billing.ts:140-175 findUserByStripeBillingIdentity pages through all users via supabaseAdmin.auth.admin.listUsers() when no userId. O(n) with user base, no max-page cap. Add a max page count (e.g., 10 pages = 2000 users) and return null with a console.warn beyond that.

title: P1: Stripe webhook event idempotency (audit 1.5)
description: Audit 1.5 (MEDIUM). app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts processes checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.deleted, and invoice.payment_failed without idempotency guards. Stripe retries can cause duplicate grantProAccessToUser calls (mostly safe but logs duplicate pro_activated events and may fire duplicate conversion pixels). Add an event.id-keyed dedupe — store processed event IDs in a new table or upsert by event.id.

title: P1: Server-side weekly big-decision counter (audit 1.4 follow-up)
description: Follow-up to audit 1.4 / beads-1np. The initial server-side limits dispatch covers the daily ask + daily today-refresh counters (sufficient for DoS protection). The weekly big-decision-bonus slot was deliberately deferred because it requires a coordinated client+server change: client must send isBigDecision: boolean in the request body, server must check + decrement the weekly counter. Touchpoints: app/api/generate-decision-guidance/route.ts request schema, components/decision-guidance-form.tsx submission body, lib/server-usage-limits.ts (extend with weekly period key).

title: P2: CI check that model IDs in code exist in pricing config (audit 4.8)
description: Audit 4.8 (CONCERN). lib/llm.ts cost estimation uses bakeoff/config/model-pricing.json with no automated check that model IDs referenced in lib/model-routing.ts and lib/model-decision.ts have pricing entries. Add a small script (scripts/verify-model-pricing.ts or similar) that walks the model maps + asserts every referenced model has a pricing row. Fail loudly. Wire into npm scripts so CI runs it; add a startup warning fallback.

title: P2: Unit test suite for safety + billing critical functions (audit 4.5)
description: Audit 4.5 (CONCERN). No unit tests despite Playwright e2e + bakeoff. Add Vitest suite for: isAtLeastAge (domain/safety/age-gate.ts), detectCrisisInput/Output (domain/safety/crisis-detection.ts), classifyOutputSafety (domain/safety/output-safety.ts), getModelRoutingDecision (lib/model-decision.ts), deriveAttributionChannel (lib/paid-media.ts), getResolvedUserAccessLevel + getDailyUsageLimits (lib/access.ts), and the new HMAC helpers (isOpsSessionValid, verifyCheckoutAccessCookie, getDailyPeriodKey, etc.). Wire into npm scripts.

title: P2: Integrate model-routing pass with model-decision useFrontier flag (audit 2.1)
description: Audit 2.1 (HIGH per audit, P2 per coordinator). Two model-selection systems run independently: getModelForPass() in lib/model-routing.ts (pass→model map) and getModelRoutingDecision() in lib/model-decision.ts (signal-based useFrontier). When they disagree, pass routing wins for compose, which can produce lower-quality output for pro users on complex days. Integrate so getModelRoutingDecision explicitly overrides or gates getModelForPass. Document precedence.

title: P2: Sign attribution cookie wuwu_attr_ft (audit 1.6)
description: Audit 1.6 (MEDIUM). The wuwu_attr_ft attribution cookie is set with httpOnly + sameSite:lax but is NOT signed. parseAttributionCookie does JSON.parse with no schema validation. Add HMAC-SHA256 signing (use OPS_SECRET as the HMAC key, similar to ops auth + checkout cookie patterns we just landed) and validate the parsed JSON against a Zod schema. Files: lib/paid-media.ts, middleware.ts (cookie setter), any reader.

title: P2: API rate limiting middleware (audit 1.2 + 3.1 combined)
description: Audit 1.2 + 3.1 (combined). 1.2: Bearer token auth has no per-route rate limit, can be brute-forced. 3.1: LLM generation endpoints (/api/generate-briefing, /api/generate-forecast, /api/generate-blueprint, /api/ask-follow-up, /api/generate-decision-guidance) have no server-side rate limiting — a free user who clears localStorage can spam unlimited generations. The new server-side daily caps from audit 1.4 cover the free-tier abuse, but we still need: (a) auth-rate-limiting for bearer-token endpoints (e.g., 60/min/user), (b) sustained-rate caps for paid users to prevent runaway LLM costs (e.g., 30 generations/hour even for pro). Coordinator owns this design — likely Upstash Redis sliding-window counters with a wrapper helper invoked from middleware or per-route. Defer to follow-up if Upstash isn't already provisioned.

title: F-06: Today card scannability — re-audit against actual structure (audit premise was stale)
description:
Original 2026-04-26 design audit said: 'today card is a wall of prose at components/today-card', restructure to headline + do/defer pair. Deferred because the premise was wrong.

Current state: there is no `components/today-card` directory. The today briefing renders inline in app/dashboard/page.tsx and is already structured into:
- Today's thesis (one-paragraph frame)
- Today's move (the actionable bit)
- Energy + pacing
- Career, Relationships, Money sections (paywalled for free users)
- A 'Systems align' concordance card (3.0.1) when systems agree
- BriefingFeedbackForm (rating chips) at the bottom
- 'See your accuracy read →' link to /accuracy
- (Now) MemoryIntroToast on first fact extraction (C-03)

What to do — re-audit against what's ACTUALLY there:
1. Boot `npm run dev` and visit /dashboard logged in as the smoke test account
2. Test mobile viewport at 375px and 414px — does anything overflow / collapse poorly?
3. Is the headline/thesis card pulling enough weight at the top?
4. Are the rating chips discoverable (BriefingFeedbackForm)?
5. Does the 'Systems align' card feel like signal or filler when present?
6. If the actual critique is about something else (long-form below thesis, paywalled section density, scroll length), fix THAT — don't rebuild a layout that already exists in spirit.

## Context
Source: ~/Downloads/design_handoff_wuwu_ux_audit/issues/F-06-today-card-unscannable.md

The original audit was working from a phantom file path. Re-audit needed before implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Documented what's actually on /dashboard (vs. the audit's phantom layout)
- [ ] Identified ≤3 specific scannability issues with severity tags
- [ ] Implemented fixes for P0/P1 issues only — leave P2 in this issue for follow-up
- [ ] Mobile 375px and 414px both render cleanly (no overflow, no orphan whitespace)
- [ ] Rating chips visible above the fold OR within one comfortable scroll
- [ ] No regression to the 'Systems align' / accuracy-link / memory-toast surfaces

title: F-09: Settings layout — polish existing /onboarding-as-settings, don't rebuild
description:
Original 2026-04-26 design audit said: settings page is the onboarding flow reused; split into four anchored sections (Account / Chart / Privacy / Notifications). Deferred because the structure already exists at lower fidelity.

Current state: no `/settings` route exists. `/onboarding` doubles as settings (correctly identified by the audit). Returning users hit /onboarding and see:
- Header with 'Profile and privacy' kicker + 'Settings' title
- OnboardingForm component with two card-featured sections: 'Account basics' and 'Birth profile'
- PrivacyDataSection below the form: links to /privacy/facts (memory), delete-account flow

So three of the four 'jobs' are already separated — the only missing one is Notifications, which doesn't exist because push/email haven't shipped (Gate 4+).

What to do:
1. Boot `npm run dev`, log in as smoke test account, visit /onboarding (acts as Settings for returning users)
2. Audit the visual hierarchy: are section breaks legible? Does PrivacyDataSection feel like a top-level concern or a footnote?
3. Recommend specific polish: anchor links, sticky sub-nav, bigger section headers, reordering — based on what the existing layout actually needs
4. Don't add a Notifications section that has nothing to control
5. Don't introduce a new /settings route — /onboarding works, just polish it

## Context
Source: ~/Downloads/design_handoff_wuwu_ux_audit/issues/F-09-settings-four-jobs.md

Audit assumed /settings exists separately. It doesn't. Polish what's there.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Audit of current /onboarding-as-settings hierarchy documented
- [ ] PrivacyDataSection (memory + delete account) reads as a top-level concern, not a footnote
- [ ] Section breaks visually distinct (heading weight, spacing, optional anchor links)
- [ ] Deep-link anchors work if added (/onboarding#chart, /onboarding#privacy)
- [ ] No new design tokens; uses existing card-featured / form-section-header patterns
- [ ] Mobile renders cleanly

title: P-04: Pricing free column — polish existing Free card, don't add one (it exists)
description:
Original 2026-04-26 design audit said: pricing page is missing a 'Free, forever' column, only shows Pro Monthly ($8/mo) and Pro Annual ($72/yr). Deferred because the column exists AND the audit's prices were wrong.

Current state: app/pricing/page.tsx + components/pricing-plans.tsx already render a 3-up structure:
- Free card with 4 features (Daily briefing, Blueprint overview, 30-day forecast snapshot, Ask 2/day) and primary 'Sign up — it's free' CTA routing to /login?mode=signup
- Pro Monthly: $14.99/mo (no trial)
- Pro Annual: $89.99/yr with 7-day free trial
- Billing toggle (Monthly / Annual) above the cards
- 'Good to know' FAQ section below

Audit's prices were wrong throughout the original pack. Real prices ($14.99 / $89.99) are now in the C-02 paywall fixes too.

What to do — polish, don't rebuild:
1. Boot `npm run dev`, visit /pricing anonymous + logged-in
2. Is the Free card visually subordinate (smaller, grayer, 'basic' feel) or does it carry equal weight?
3. Is the price comparison clear? Does the 7-day-trial-on-annual-only disclosure surface cleanly?
4. Are the 4 free-tier benefits the right 4 (matches actual free-tier behavior — 3 Ask/day + 1 weekly Big Decision per the 3.0.2 ship)?
5. Mobile stack order — does the Free column come first (anchor) or last?
6. Match copy to actual product behavior: '3 Ask questions per day + 1 weekly Big Decision' (not the stale '2 questions per day' in pricing-plans.tsx)

## Context
Source: ~/Downloads/design_handoff_wuwu_ux_audit/issues/P-04-pricing-free-forever.md

Audit pack used wrong prices throughout ($8/$72) and assumed a missing column that exists. This is a polish pass, not an addition.

Pricing reference (use these everywhere):
- Pro Monthly: $14.99/mo, no trial
- Pro Annual: $89.99/yr, 7-day free trial
- Free: no expiry, 3 Ask/day + 1 Big Decision/week
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Free card carries equal visual weight to Pro cards
- [ ] Free-tier feature list matches actual product (3 Ask/day + 1 Big Decision/wk, NOT '2 questions per day')
- [ ] 7-day trial on annual surfaces clearly; 'no trial on monthly' is honest, not buried
- [ ] Mobile stack order is sensible
- [ ] No reference to wrong prices ($8/mo, $72/yr) anywhere

title: F-05: Birth-time precision — verify existing 'I don't know' branch covers the spec
description:
Original 2026-04-26 design audit said: add an 'I don't know my birth time' checkbox + chart-fidelity flag, helper text under the field. Deferred from the audit-pack implementation pass because the premise was likely stale.

Current state: a `birthTimeConfidence` selector already exists in components/onboarding-form.tsx, fed by `BIRTH_TIME_CONFIDENCE_OPTIONS` from lib/config.ts. We did not verify whether the existing options cover an 'unknown' / 'not sure' branch, or whether downstream chart rendering (Blueprint house labels, Forecast house references, Today house-based content) suppresses house-based content gracefully when confidence is low.

What to do:
1. Read lib/config.ts to confirm the actual values in BIRTH_TIME_CONFIDENCE_OPTIONS
2. Test the onboarding flow with an 'unknown' / 'low confidence' selection
3. Check Blueprint, Forecast, and Today renders — do house-based sections render with empty/broken content, or are they suppressed?
4. Identify the actual delta vs. the F-05 spec — UI affordance, server flag, downstream rendering
5. Implement only the gap; don't rebuild what's already there

## Context
Source: ~/Downloads/design_handoff_wuwu_ux_audit/issues/F-05-birth-time-precision.md

Original audit's premise about a missing 'I don't know' branch may be wrong — birthTimeConfidence already exists. This task is verify-then-implement-the-actual-gap, not blind implementation of the spec.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Confirmed BIRTH_TIME_CONFIDENCE_OPTIONS values + their semantic meaning
- [ ] Helper text under the birth-time field explains why precision matters (per F-05 spec: 'To the hour is enough. We use this to place the houses.')
- [ ] Low-confidence path tested end-to-end — flag stored, downstream renders adapt
- [ ] No house-based content rendered as broken/empty for users with low birth-time confidence
- [ ] Existing high-confidence users unaffected
- [ ] No new chart_fidelity flag if birthTimeConfidence is sufficient — reuse, don't duplicate
